Hi Priya, Karthik — quick technical follow-up from our infra bench perspective. Thanks for the CSV, it’s helpful. A few items I want to confirm so the pilot sizing is accurate: 

1) Tokenization details: are you using a BPE model compatible with standard GPT-like tokenizers? If you can confirm the tokenizer family or share a sanitized example we’ll run identical tokenization.
2) Streaming concurrency model: do you open a persistent websocket per session (long-lived) or do you re-negotiate on each user message? Long-lived WebSockets change how we account for KV cache memory per connection.
3) Crest windows: you said 5-10 minutes — can you confirm the expected crest QPS distribution (e.g., 3k QPS for 10% of minutes each hour or a single 5–10 min spike only when campaign runs?) We’ll use a crest duty-cycle assumption in our capacity model.

Prelim numbers from our side (very conservative until we run your examples):
- For chat short replies (~160 tokens avg, p95 < 800ms): estimate 450 steady QPS per dedicated GPU, peak crest handling 1.8k QPS with autoscale burst.
- If average response moves to ~700 tokens frequently, throughput drops — expect ~120 steady QPS per GPU for that workload if using the same model family (unquantized).
- Streaming concurrency: for long-lived websocket sessions we budget ~18MB of KV state per active session (varies by model/seq-length). 2.5k concurrent sessions would therefore require significant KV memory; we can provide a compact quantized variant to reduce memory.

Next actions: once we have the populated snapshot and a couple of sample payloads we’ll run a tokenization pass and provide a short SLO vs cost tradeoff matrix (p50/p95 buckets with suggested model variants and quantization). Also happy to do a short benchmarking run using your samples in our staging tenant.
